- When sentiment shows strong positive spikes (≥0.67) followed by sharp declines, model tends to overreact and overshoot — reduce forecast by 5–10% in next 3–5 days.  
- If sentiment is consistently negative (≤0.33) over 3+ days, model underestimates — add 3–7% to forecast to account for mean reversion.  
- After a sharp price drop, model often fails to capture rebound — if sentiment turns positive within 2 days, adjust forecast upward by 2–5% to reflect momentum.  
- If news volume is low (0.0) but sentiment is high, model overestimates — reduce forecast by 3–8% to avoid sentiment-overdrive bias.  
- Model consistently underpredicts in 30-day horizon when sentiment is volatile (±0.33 change over 3+ days) — apply smoothing filter or add 1–3% to forecast.  
- Overshoots after sentiment spikes are common — if forecast > true outcome by >5%, reduce next forecast by 5–10% to correct for lagged reaction.  
- If sentiment is flat (±0.00) for 3+ days, model tends to drift — apply mean reversion rule: forecast = 0.8×previous + 0.2×true recent value.
